questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select no substitution required

The banquet hall __is been renovate__ recently.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 
• The word 'recently' indicates that the action has been performed not long ago. In this case we use the **present perfect tense** which means an action that has just been performed in the past and has a link with the present.
 
• The option which is in the present perfect tense is **'has been renovated'.**
 
• So, only option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A person who has had long experience in a particular field
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1) i.e. Veteran.**

 
• **Veteran means a person who has had long experience in a particular field.**
 
• Amateur means a person who engages in a pursuit, especially a sport, on an unpaid rather than a professional basis.
 
• Cosmopolitan means including people from many different countries.
 
• Stoic means a person who can endure pain or hardship without showing their feelings or complaining.
 
• So, only option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. who.**

We need to use the correct pronoun in the blank. Let us look at the usage of all the mentioned pronouns:

 
• Which is used in asking for information specifying one or more people or things from a definite set.
 
• Whom is used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• That is used to identify a specific person or thing observed or heard by the speaker.
 
• **Who** is used to introduce a clause giving further information about a person or people previously mentioned.

The most appropriate word is 'who' as it is used to refer to the young boy in the news.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. from.**

Let us look at the usage of the prepositions-

 
• At means 'present in a specific location or the time when an event takes place'.
 
• **From** means 'indicating the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts'.
 
• For means 'the time for which an action is performed'.
 
• To means 'indicating the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts'.

The most appropriate word is 'from' as it indicates that he returned from the jungle.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.

The closest word to 'utter something' is **'say'.**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select no substitution required

More than 60% of India’s population __live under the poverty line.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"lives below the poverty line".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject **"India’s population" **is singular; therefore, the verb should also be singular.
 
• The original sentence uses **"live," **which is plural.
 
• The correct form should be **"lives."**
 
• The correct preposition to use when referring to the level at which people are considered poor is **"below" **the poverty line, not **"under."**
 
• The phrase **"below the poverty line" **is a standard expression used to describe the threshold below which individuals or families are considered to be living in poverty.
 
• The use of the singular verb **"lives" **along with the correct preposition **"below" **correctly matches the subject and appropriately conveys the intended meaning.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 "lives beside the poverty line" changes the meaning entirely, suggesting proximity rather than an economic condition.
 
 
• "Beside" means at the side of or next to.
 
 
 
• Option 2 "no substitution required" is incorrect because the original usage of "live under the poverty line" is not standard and the verb tense does not match the singular subject.
 
• Option 3 "live by the poverty line" also changes the meaning, suggesting living according to the poverty line rather than beneath it in economic terms.
 
 
• "By" can mean close to or according to, which does not fit the intended context.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

David and me are brothers but from different mothers.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3 i.e. David and me.**

 
• The pronoun 'me' is used when the person is an object in the sentence. Here **'David and me' is the subject** of the sentence. We cannot use 'me' in this situation.
 
• The **correct pronoun in this case is 'I'**.
 
• So, the correct phrase is **'David and I'.**
 
• **Corrected sentence: **David and I are brothers but from different mothers.
